title: Python SDK dependencies: generated standard-library dataclasses, a Go wheel writer and unittest (replaces pydantic, hatchling, pytest, Pillow and the separate runtime wheel)
The harness is Go; the Python client stays Python, pure and thin
Wire types and method stubs are generated into standard-library dataclasses; pydantic is removed
Host requests go to typed handlers; there is no generic reverse-request queue
The Go binary ships inside per-platform wheels of one distribution; nothing is downloaded
Wheels are written by a Go tool in the release job
The Python API is redesigned: the model is kept, the names and types change
Office operations and resource downloads leave the Python package
A tool defined in Python is a host-registered tool answered over the same connection
A pure-Python client that starts, drives and stops the harness
Python wire types and method stubs generated from the protocol schema
Platform wheels that carry the Go binary, written by a Go tool
The installed binary is found, checked and runnable as dsh
A Python function can be offered to the model as a tool
Framing and correlation: concurrent requests, whole-line writes, reported malformed lines, and a host request never completes a pending call
Lifecycle: lazy start, handshake timeout with diagnostics, a request timeout that cancels nothing, and every rung of the close ladder
No launch without an explicit home, and a provider key only in the child environment
Approval and question handlers: worker threads, cancellation, late answers, errors, unknown methods and derived capability flags
run() returns on the host's completion notice; overlapping runs stay separate; a slow consumer fails alone and recovers from history
A protocol version mismatch stops the child; a build version mismatch fails only for the bundled binary
Regenerating the Python protocol module from the checked-in schema gives the checked-in file
Sample messages written from Go values decode and re-encode equally in Python; malformed input raises one protocol error
The Python package needs nothing outside the standard library and contains no Office module
The wheel writer produces a correctly named, hashed, repeatable archive and refuses a wrong payload, size or version
Every release target has one wheel row, and a binary that does not match its tag is refused
The binary is resolved in a fixed order, a damaged install is named, and verify_runtime() detects a changed byte
The dsh console command forwards arguments, environment and exit code on POSIX and Windows
Tools declared in Python are advertised, dispatched to their function, cancelled and reported
An installed wheel drives a real model through approval, cancel, restart and resume
On every target a real installer selects a wheel whose binary runs and verifies
A killed host and a killed client leave no orphan and an honest session
A real model calls a tool defined in Python

reason: The Python client is kept as a pure-Python subprocess client with the same model (lazy start, sessions, run results, approvals, questions, close ladder), but it is redesigned: types are generated from the protocol schema, the run result and notification scoping come from the host, and approvals become a callback.

The carrier package for a single-file Node executable is replaced by platform wheels of the one distribution that hold the ordinary Go dsh binary; the 159-entry closure manifest, the Node bootstrap, the sidecars and the download manifest have no counterpart.

pydantic validates hand-mirrored wire models at the boundary; the Go design generates frozen standard-library dataclasses with decode and encode functions from the SDK protocol schema, which keeps the boundary check and removes the dependency and the second copy of the types.

hatchling and its custom hook build and tag the wheels; in the Go design a Go tool in the release job writes every wheel from the cross-compiled binaries and keeps the hook's payload, tag and size checks.

pytest runs the client's tests; the Go design's Python tests use the standard-library unittest runner so that the package needs no third-party Python package at test time, and product behaviour that upstream tests through Python is tested in Go.
Pillow is a test-only dependency that draws and inspects images for the Office render check; Office operations leave the Python package, so nothing in it needs an image library.
The separate runtime distribution and its exact version pin are folded into one distribution whose platform wheels contain the Go binary, with a pure fallback wheel for platforms that have none.

Kept: the wheels are installed into a fresh environment outside the checkout, identity (imported from the install, binary inside it, matching versions, verified hash) is proven before any behaviour, a keyless installer scenario runs on every target and a real-model scenario runs on trusted runs where a missing key fails.

The proposal's premise is false at the pinned commit: the SDK server sends approval/request and user-question/ask as requests (packages/sdk/server/src/server.ts:138, packages/sdk/server/src/user-questions.ts:48), so a one-directional client would lose approvals. Its intent is met another way: the generic next_request, respond, respond_error and notify API is removed in favour of typed handlers, and a frame with an id and a method can never complete a pending call.

title: The Python runtime wheel ships the whole Node application as one executable, and a build pipeline (813 lines of scripts, a 159-entry closure manifest, a patched packer, sidecars, a 530-line workflow) exists only to make it

reason: The Go binary is already one static file cross-compiled for every target, so the wheel carries the release binary unchanged and the packer, closure manifest, deploy step, bootstrap and sidecars are not needed.

title: The SDK wire types are mirrored by hand in Python and must be changed in two places

reason: The Python types and method stubs are generated from the one protocol schema, and a test fails when the generated file is stale.

title: The Python client re-derives the run result, the session tree and command completion from the raw event stream

reason: The host scopes notifications and sends the run result, and the client is held to a rule of no product logic in Python, so the interval, tree and pairing code is not rebuilt.

title: Approvals need a caller-written loop over a generic request queue while questions use a callback, and the client's queues are unbounded

reason: Every host request is dispatched to a typed handler on a bounded number of worker threads, and each run and subscription has a bounded buffer whose overflow fails only that consumer.

title: The packaged executable switches between five process roles by environment variable, and the Python runtime package doubles as a resource downloader with its own cache

reason: The wheel holds the ordinary dsh binary with no Python-specific entry point, and the Python package downloads nothing and manages no cache.

title: A development-only Node carrier (DSH_RUNTIME_MODE=node) is a second way to run the runtime and must be excluded from every wheel

reason: The second carrier exists only because the runtime is a Node program that can also run unpacked on a system Node; a Go binary has one form, and a developer points dsh_bin at a local build.

title: Runtime wheels cover five targets, each built on its own native runner, with no Windows arm64 and a conservative macOS floor, because of native Node addons

reason: One pure-Go binary per release target is built from one runner, the wheel set follows the release targets, and a test refuses a tag that does not match the binary's header.
